title: Scaling AI in Education: A Khanmigo case study: Shawn Jansepar

domains.label: Education & Learning
domains.rationale: The talk centers on Khanmigo as an AI education product, covering UX design for Socratic tutoring, human-in-the-loop teacher tools, trust/safety in classrooms, and how students and teachers collaborate with the system. Khanmigo is a tutoring and learning product serving students and teachers across school districts and individual subscribers. The case study traces Khanmigo from rapid prototyping through production launch alongside GPT-4 to ongoing scaling and iteration. The presentation mixes product demos with moderate technical depth accessible to a general AI engineering audience. Recorded live conference presentation at the AI Engineer World's Fair. All evidence anchors are graded as said_in_transcript with direct excerpts from the talk.

summary:
Shawn Jansepar, Director of Engineering at Khan Academy and product leader of the Khanmigo Platform, discusses scaling AI in education through Khanmigo, covering problems solved, demos, organizational transformation, technical challenges, and scaling strategies. Khan Academy is a nonprofit with 140 million registered users, 7 billion learning minutes (2021-2022), 1.5 million highly active learners, and approximately 200,000 paid Khanmigo users split between school districts and individual subscribers, targeting historically underresourced learners.

Post-pandemic, average eighth graders are 1.1 grade levels behind. Khan Academy views AI as a tool to democratize one-on-one tutoring at scale. Khanmigo serves as both a tutor for learners and an assistant for teachers, using a Socratic approach that avoids giving away answers, improved math accuracy, deep integration with Khan Academy content, and specialized UX affordances.

The transformation to an AI-first organization relied on rapid prototyping inspired by "Creative Selection," pairing builders with domain experts, resisting perfectionism, and trusting intuition. Khan Academy updated core values and product development processes to support tiered code quality based on confidence levels. The OpenAI partnership began with AP Biology questions, progressed through red teaming and reinforcement learning with embedded content team members, and culminated in a company-wide hackathon to launch alongside GPT-4.

Technical challenges include tutor accuracy improvements via a math agent, Chain of Thought prompting, RAG with step-by-step solutions, and a tutoring accuracy dashboard. Prompt engineering evolved from spaghetti code to a component architecture with defined inputs/outputs, minimal viable test coverage, and Langfuse tracing. The team found model-graded evals catch math mistakes roughly 70% of the time compared to human labels.

Scaling challenges require Khanmigo to be reliable, affordable for lower-income districts, and fast enough to avoid user frustration. Solutions include leveraging multiple models, fallback to shared capacity, perceived performance improvements, Microsoft Azure compute donations, and evaluation of efficient models like GPT-4o and Phi-3. Microsoft is building Phi-3.14, a small-to-medium language model optimized for math tutoring. Future plans include load balancing between OpenAI and Azure for redundancy and dynamic scaling.

sections.title: Introduction and Khan Academy Mission
sections.summary: Shawn introduces himself as Director of AI and Learning at Khan Academy. Khan Academy is a nonprofit with 140M registered users, 7B learning minutes, 1.5M active learners, and 200K paid Khanmigo users. The organization targets historically underresourced learners.

sections.title: Learning Gaps and Khanmigo Vision
sections.summary: Post-pandemic, average 8th graders are 1.1 grade levels behind. Khan Academy believes AI can democratize one-on-one tutoring. Khanmigo serves as tutor for learners and assistant for teachers. Emulating tutors has been their North Star; LLMs accelerate toward that vision.

sections.title: Khanmigo vs ChatGPT and Platform Integration
sections.summary: Demonstrates Khanmigo's Socratic approach versus ChatGPT's answer-giving behavior, and math accuracy improvements. Shows integration into platform content with contextual tutoring. Discusses UX affordances important for education beyond traditional chat interfaces.

sections.title: Writing Coach Demonstration
sections.summary: Shows writing coach breaking essay writing into outlining, drafting, and revision. AI refuses to write content for students, provides iterative feedback, preserves conversation history for teacher validation, and flags text that appears without provenance.

sections.title: Teacher Tools and Classroom Integration
sections.summary: Covers teacher tools including classroom snapshots, moderation features, skills reports, progress report generation, lesson planning, and exit tickets. Microsoft sponsored these tools for free US teacher access. Tight feedback loop between student activity and teacher insights.

sections.title: Classroom Video and Building Khanmigo
sections.summary: Shows a video of Khanmigo in a 6th grade classroom. Discusses transformation to AI-first through rapid prototyping inspired by Creative Selection. OpenAI partnership began with AP Bio questions, progressed through red teaming, and planned a company-wide hackathon to launch alongside GPT-4.

sections.title: Keys to Success and Organizational Change
sections.summary: Keys to success included resisting perfectionism, making quick reversible decisions for two-way door decisions while thinking deeply about one-way door decisions like trust and safety, trusting intuition, leveraging learning scientist expertise, rapid iteration with demo-driven development, and fixed timelines to avoid Parkinson's law. Khan Academy introduced Organization Decision Records and updated core values to include trusting intuition and resisting perfectionism.

sections.title: Product Development Process and AI Platform Team
sections.summary: Replaced heavyweight agile process with tiered code quality framework: scrappy prototypes for low-confidence features, AB/beta tests for medium confidence, and higher quality with accessibility checklists for full-release features. Added an AI platform team as glue between infrastructure and product teams, owning the AI developer experience, component interface in Go with automatic Langfuse tracing, AI router, chat component APIs, and Khanmigo-as-a-service for third-party embedding.

sections.title: Technical Hurdles: Tutor Accuracy
sections.summary: Improved tutor accuracy via a math agent with calculator and Python access, Chain of Thought prompting that writes out how the student arrived at an answer and how it should be solved before tutoring, RAG with step-by-step solutions, and a tutoring accuracy dashboard to monitor quality and prevent regressions. Next steps include releasing a math accuracy benchmark dataset with a paper, Wolfram integration, and fine-tuning.

sections.title: Prompt Engineering Evolution
sections.summary: Prompt engineering evolved from spaghetti code with varied test coverage to a refactored component architecture with defined inputs/outputs. Now developing minimal viable test coverage across all activities, manual test tools with humans in the loop, moving toward model-graded evals. All stack traces available in Langfuse. Model-graded evals catch math mistakes roughly 70% of the time versus human labels. Adding more languages risks ballooning complexity.

sections.title: Scale, Performance, and Cost
sections.summary: Khanmigo must be reliable, cheap enough for lower-income districts, and fast enough to avoid frustration. Solutions include multiple models in production, fallback to shared capacity, perceived performance UI improvements, and Microsoft Azure compute donations. Evaluating GPT-4o, Phi-3, and Phi-3.14 (Microsoft's math-tutoring-optimized small model). Future plans include OpenAI/Azure load balancing for redundancy and dynamic scaling to use compute more efficiently. Shawn closes by challenging the audience to leverage AI to enhance human potential.
